Stage 4.0A - Expanded experiment evaluation

Generated 2026-11-19 10:53 UTC. Read-only audit of eight experiments. No training, inference, regenerated predictions, protected-file edits or locked-test access.

Rules applied

Metrics stay inside their own evaluation partition and target transformation. There is no cross-experiment ranking: each section has its own tables and axes.
The train_mse_scaled / validation_mse_scaled histories belong to the Mendeley tabular MLP (E1, E2, E3): MSE on a standardized total-project duration. Cambridge GraphSAGE histories (E8) are L1 on log1p(activity days). The two are never merged.
Synthetic results (E4) come from labels generated by a known rule. They test the pipeline and are not evidence of real-world predictive accuracy.
Stage 2.3E held-out numbers were computed on the same 99 locked blocks that Stage 3.7 protects. This audit shows only the stored aggregate, never re-derives it, and never compares it with development results.

Chronological overview

Order follows the documented stage labels: Mendeley tabular models, Cambridge classical models, the synthetic and DSLIB graph experiments, then Cambridge GraphSAGE. File timestamps conflict with this order for the Stage 3.5 checkpoints, so they are listed but not used.

E1 - Mendeley tabular MLP - single held-out split

Stage 1 (duration v1)models/duration_v1

Research objective
Predict total project duration (ProjDura) from nine physical project descriptors with a small MLP, as the first PMI duration model.
Dataset and features
Mendeley tabular dataset. 40 training rows (32 fitting, 8 inner validation, grouped by project name) and a separate 10-row test file. Features: AreaSite, BuiltArea, TowerNum, TowerHgt, TowerFlr, BasementNum, AreaBase, UnitNum, AreaUnit. Cost columns excluded. Two different records named Pr29 remain grouped. Duration unit unverified.
Target transformation
ProjDura (total project duration, unit unverified), StandardScaler on fitting rows
Loss
MSE on standardized ProjDura (train_mse_scaled / validation_mse_scaled)
Evaluation partition
Inner validation = 8 rows (GroupShuffleSplit seed 42); final metric on 10-row test file
Training and validation
One grouped fitting/validation split (seed 42). Imputer, feature scaler and target scaler fitted on the 32 fitting rows only. Best inner-validation epoch restored; no refit on all 40 rows. The 10 test rows were used once for final evaluation.
Maximum and executed epochs
Maximum 2,000. Executed 2000. Restored epoch 1957.
Best checkpoint and stopping
Lowest inner-validation scaled MSE (0.2332) at epoch 1957. Patience did not trigger; the run hit the epoch cap.

Convergence, overfitting or underfitting

Inner-validation loss fell from 1.395 to 0.233 and was still falling at the cap (drop over the last 200 epochs 0.1772). Training loss ended at 0.020, about a tenth of the validation loss, so the 305-parameter network fits its 32 rows far more closely than unseen rows. Validation loss never turned upward, so there is no classic overfitting turn within budget, but convergence was not reached: the stopping rule never fired.

Research limitations

  • Only 8 validation rows and 10 test rows; R2 of 0.866 on 10 rows is weak evidence.
  • Later grouped CV (E3) gave mean MLP R2 of -0.28, so the single-split result did not generalise.
  • Input hashes in metrics.json were recorded under another machine path; current files still match.
  • Total-project duration; not an activity-level or IFC-change delay estimate.

Reason for moving to the next experiment

A single 10-row test cannot separate model quality from split luck. Grouped repeated CV on the development rows (E2/E3) was the next step.

Convergence, overfitting or underfitting

Loss histories, checkpoints, fold CSVs and predictions are SHA-256 identical to E3 repeat 1 (verified file by file, not by size). Convergence is assessed under E3.

Research limitations

  • Duplicate evidence: E2 adds no independent information beyond E3 repeat 1.
  • fold_manifest.json input hashes were recorded on another machine path.

Reason for moving to the next experiment

One repeat gives a single grouping of 40 rows. E3 added two further shuffles to show grouping variance.

E3 - Mendeley grouped 5-fold CV, 3 repeats

Stage 1 development validation (3 repeats)data/processed/duration_validation_repeated

Research objective
Measure how stable the Mendeley MLP, ridge and mean baselines are across three different project groupings.
Dataset and features
40 Mendeley development rows, nine features; 10-row test file never loaded. 24-26 fitting, 7-8 inner validation and 7-9 evaluation rows per fold.
Target transformation
ProjDura, StandardScaler on each fold's fitting rows
Loss
MSE on standardized ProjDura (train_mse_scaled / validation_mse_scaled)
Evaluation partition
Outer grouped 5-fold evaluation folds x 3 repeats (seeds 42/43/44)
Training and validation
3 repeats x GroupKFold(5) with seeds 42, 43, 44. Inner grouped validation chooses the MLP epoch; outer rows never select anything. Preprocessing and baselines fitted on inner fitting rows only.
Maximum and executed epochs
Maximum 2,000 per fold. Executed 185-1620. Restored epochs 35-1470 (median 251).
Best checkpoint and stopping
Patience 150 triggered in all 15 runs (executed = restored + 150). Lowest inner-validation scaled MSE restored.

Convergence, overfitting or underfitting

All 15 runs stopped by patience. In 15 of 15 runs the inner-validation loss rose after the restored epoch while training loss kept falling (median further train drop 0.168), the classic overfitting signature on 7-8 validation rows. Inner-validation MSE at the restored epoch ranges 0.05-2.97 (scaled units), so stopping is driven by very small, noisy validation sets.

Research limitations

  • 40 records; folds share training rows, so SDs are variation, not confidence intervals.
  • MLP mean MAE 6.48 vs ridge 6.25 vs mean 7.26: no model explains variance (R2 < 0).
  • Unit and source licence unverified; repeated Pr29 identity unresolved.

Reason for moving to the next experiment

Project-level tabular data was too small to support a neural model. Work moved to activity-level schedule data (Cambridge, DSLIB) with many more labelled rows.

E4 - Duration GNN - synthetic schedules

Stage 3.5models/gnn_synthetic

Synthetic data. Pipeline test only. Not evidence of real-world accuracy.
Research objective
Check that the graph pipeline can learn a neighbour-dependent effect when one is planted. A pipeline test, not a result.
Dataset and features
120 projects in 120 independent groups, 2,510 labelled activities. 22 planning-time node features (CPM start/float, critical flag, degree, depth, project size, 12 trade one-hot). Labels follow a known synthetic rule.
Target transformation
log(actual_days / planned_days); reported in days via planned x exp(pred)
Loss
Huber (delta 0.5) on log ratio - per-epoch values NOT saved
Evaluation partition
5-fold project-grouped OOF; 15% of training groups for early stopping
Training and validation
5-fold cross-validation over project groups; 15% of training groups held out for early stopping; scaling fitted on training nodes. Baselines: plan, global median ratio, per-category median ratio, NodeMLP. Paired bootstrap (2,000) over projects against the best non-graph method.
Maximum and executed epochs
Maximum 150 per fold. Executed and per-fold best epochs were printed to the console only and not saved.
Best checkpoint and stopping
Lowest early-stopping Huber loss, patience 30, best state restored. The saved model.pt is a separate refit on all projects for the median CV best epoch.

Convergence, overfitting or underfitting

No per-epoch history was saved, so convergence, overfitting and underfitting cannot be assessed from curves. Out-of-fold error is low and consistent across folds, which shows the model fits the planted rule without obvious overfitting.

Research limitations

Reason for moving to the next experiment

Convergence, overfitting or underfitting

No per-epoch history was saved, so convergence, overfitting and underfitting cannot be assessed from curves. Out-of-fold, both neural models are worse than 'actual = planned'. With most labels exactly on plan, this is consistent with fitting noise rather than signal.

Research limitations

  • Only 17 independent groups; labels dominated by on-plan values.
  • 22% of activity names match no trade; FS/SS/FF/SF treated as FS in CPM features; lags ignored.
  • No learning curves or per-fold best epochs saved; model.pt is not the fold model.

Reason for moving to the next experiment

No model beat the plan. A filtered sensitivity run (E6) checked whether tracking artefacts explained this.

Convergence, overfitting or underfitting

No per-epoch history was saved, so convergence, overfitting and underfitting cannot be assessed from curves. Same pattern as E5; per-project MAE is worse for GNN than MLP (6.80 vs 6.38).

Research limitations

Reason for moving to the next experiment

Filtering did not change the conclusion. Too few independent groups; the larger Cambridge dataset with a frozen protocol became the main test bed (E8, building on E7).

E7 - Cambridge classical models (median, ridge, random forest, MLP)

Stage 2.3Edata/processed/stage2/cambridge_experiment (+ models/cambridge_duration_v1)

Research objective
Exploratory retrospective estimates of reported completed-activity elapsed calendar days on Cambridge JPF data with non-graph models, under the frozen Stage 2.3D protocol.
Dataset and features
Cambridge JPF export. Features: activity_description, project_type, uk_region only. 144,110 development rows in 70 conservative blocks; 36,027 locked test rows in 99 blocks (not opened by this audit).
Target transformation
Raw reported elapsed calendar days (no log); MLP target standardized
Loss
MLP: MSE on standardized days (train), L1 on standardized days (stopping) - NOT saved
Evaluation partition
5 frozen development folds; historical held-out summary on 99 locked blocks kept separate
Training and validation
Five frozen development folds (fold 0 = the dominant 99,636-row block). Ridge alpha selected per fold on a 10% inner block subset. Model order by mean development macro-group MAE, locked before the single held-out evaluation in Stage 2.3E.
Maximum and executed epochs
MLP maximum 100 per fold. Executed and best epochs were not saved.
Best checkpoint and stopping
MLP: lowest L1 on standardized days over inner 10% development blocks, patience 10.

Model architecture

Hyperparameters

parametervalue
ridgelsqr, max_iter 2000, alpha by fold [10,10,10,10,1]
random forest120 trees, max_depth 24, min_samples_leaf 4, max_features 0.6
MLP128-64-32-1, dropout .25/.15, AdamW lr 1e-3, wd 1e-3, batch 2048
MLP lossMSE on standardized days; stop on L1
MLP max epochs / patience100 / 10
textTF-IDF 50k (1,2)-gram, min_df 2, max_df .98, sublinear
dense projectionTruncatedSVD 128 + StandardScaler
seed23051

Convergence, overfitting or underfitting

No learning curves were saved for the MLP, so convergence cannot be assessed. RF and ridge are non-iterative in this sense.

Research limitations

  • Target is reported elapsed calendar days, not verified working durations.
  • Development folds are highly unequal; fold 0 is one block of 99,636 rows.
  • The 99 locked blocks were already evaluated once in Stage 2.3E and must not be reused for confirmation.
  • Prediction-time provenance of features is unverified.

Reason for moving to the next experiment

No non-graph model clearly beat the median. The next question was whether precedence-network context adds signal, under a matched-arm protocol on development folds only (E8).

E8 - Cambridge GraphSAGE vs matched no-graph network

Stage 3.7models/gnn_cambridge

Research objective
Test, under a frozen pre-registered protocol, whether GraphSAGE message passing over the exported precedence network reduces error versus an identical network with no edges.
Dataset and features
Same 144,110 development rows / 70 blocks as E7, as 163 project graphs (all exported activities are nodes; only eligible development rows labelled). 139 node inputs. Locked test projects never materialised.
Target transformation
log1p(days); predictions expm1 and clipped at 0; 3-seed mean of log predictions
Loss
L1 on log1p(days) (train_l1_log, inner_stop_l1_log, outer_val_l1_log_monitor_only)
Evaluation partition
5 frozen development folds x 3 seeds; inner stopping blocks; outer fold monitor only
Training and validation
5 frozen development folds x 3 seeds per arm. Inner stopping blocks chosen by the Stage 2.3E hash rule. Outer fold loss logged for curves only. Primary metric mean block MAE over 70 blocks; paired 2,000-sample block bootstrap.
Maximum and executed epochs
Maximum 150 per run. Executed 16-60; restored 1-45. GraphSAGE total 453 epochs, no-graph 531.
Best checkpoint and stopping
Lowest inner-stopping L1, patience 15, best restored. All 30 runs stopped by patience. 7 runs restored epoch 1-4.

Convergence, overfitting or underfitting

Training L1 keeps falling while inner-stopping L1 plateaus within roughly 5-15 epochs; at the restored epoch the outer-fold L1 exceeds training L1 by a median 0.136. This indicates weak between-block signal and mild overfitting after early epochs, controlled by early stopping. The outer-fold monitor curve is nearly flat after the first epochs.

Research limitations

  • Development-only; the 99 locked blocks were not evaluated and must not be used to confirm this result.
  • Gain is concentrated in small blocks; activity MAE improves only 0.55 days; R2 about 0; RMSE about 100 days.
  • Seed spread is comparable to the effect; the bootstrap excludes seed uncertainty.
  • training_runs.csv shows 7 runs restoring epoch 1-4; cambridge_training_results.md says four and lists five. The saved run table is authoritative.
  • Executed protocol differs from the Stage 3.7B proposal (TF-IDF/SVD not hashing, 2 layers not 3, L1 on log1p not Huber, 150/15 not 200/30, 3 seeds not 5).
  • Exported precedence may include execution-period edits; relation types merged, lags omitted, cycles retained.

Reason for moving to the next experiment

The development criterion was met with a small effect. The next stage needs a confirmatory design that does not reuse the already-used locked blocks, plus verified labels and planning-time edge provenance.

Checkpoint metadata and hashes

Identity is decided by SHA-256, never by size. The three Stage 3.5 model.pt files are all 232,503 bytes but have different hashes and different source metadata. PyTorch files were loaded with weights_only=True; joblib files were hashed but not unpickled.
